newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Immobel 1996 results seen better.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Immobel 1996 results seen better.

text.p: Belgian real estate firm Immobel will on Tuesday report an improvement in its 1996 results but will still not be in a position to resume paying a dividend, sector analysts said on Monday.
"I expect a positive net income for 1996. The first half showed a sharp improvement compared with a very poor 1995," analyst Herman Van Der Loos of Banque Bruxelles Lambert said.
"But I don't expect a very sharp improvement," he added.
Alexandre Schmitz of Bank Degroof was slightly more positive, but said this was mainly due to a good contribution from Dutch property firm Wereldhave.
"Wereldhave will contribute 88.4 million francs to the net current figure," Schmitz said.

Analysts said that while there were signs that the Brussels property market was beginning to pick up after the slump, it was slow going in general and particularly so in the construction sector on which Immobel was focused.
"No big construction sites were sold or relet in 1996. Construction is the only thing that has kept turnover stable, but with very thin margins," Van Der Loos said.
"And there is nothing exciting for Immobel in property development," he added.
"There is stabilization in the Brussels real estate market, but it is not the time to be investing in companies in the sector yet," said Schmitz, who in November upgraded Immobel to hold from sell.
He noted that Immobel had a number of projects under way which had been financed through equity.
These, he said, could either prove very healthy for the company or very dangerous for it.
"It is too early to tell. It is better to wait for a while," he said.
Neither Van Der Loos nor Schmitz could explain the recent and sudden surge in the Immobel share price.
The share has risen in almost a straight line since January 7 having fallen consistently since 1994 -- the last year on which the firm paid a share dividend.
"It could be on speculation there will be a dividend for 1996, but I don't expect there to be one," Van Der Loos said.

"The fundamentals seem to be improving, but not yet much in the property sector, and low interest rates really benefit companies like Immobel. So there is nothing specific there for Immobel," he added.

Schmitz agreed. "The recent share rise is inexplicable," he said. "I don't understand why it has gone up so much. At this stage I don't think there will be a dividend for 1996, although I do think there will be one in 1997," he said.

In 1995 Immobel recorded a group net loss of 368 million francs, after an extraordinary loss of 506 million, with turnover amounting to 6.8 billion francs. Consolidated pre-tax current profit fell to 328 million from 642 million in 1994.
In the first half of 1996 the firm reported a current profit of 85.9 million francs on a turnover of 3.9 billion francs.
At 1500 GMT the share was 10 francs up at 2,550 francs.
